Basic information that your employer will need to know about you and to reach you. Click “i” for more information.
Personal Information

The first thing your employer should see when looking at your CV is your name. Make sure it is clear, stands out, and is easy to read. Your CV should include your full address, contact phone numbers, and an e-mail address that incorporates your first and last name.

What are you looking for in a job? Is it something specific? Or is it more broad? Click “i” for more information.
Job Objective

An objective can simply be an occupational field or profession, or it can be more elaborate and contain the title or function desired, skills that you can bring to the position, and the results that the employer can expect.

Example:

A systems design position requiring my proven abilities in creative problem solving, organization, communication and follow through to provide excellent products within time constraints.

How can you best briefly describe your qualifications in a brief manner?(Optional) .Click “i” for more information.
Summary

The summary or background summary concisely elaborates on your qualifications. Typically one to two sentences in length, the summary lends credibility to the objective. This could include: who you are - years of experience (if any) - your field - three major skills - three major traits.

The aim of the summary statement is to provide the potential employer (or business partner) with a brief description of what you can do and why it is worthwhile to get to know you. It may be the basis for deciding to call you for an interview. It may determine whether the reader will continue reading your CV or not!

Example 1:

Over 11 years of progressively responsible staff and project management experience, with an earned reputation for meeting time and budget goals through better staff management, setting priorities, and teamwork.

Example 2:

An achiever with a track record of management and leadership in school clubs. Possesses excellent skills in problem solving, planning and fund raising. Resourceful, works well under pressure and delivers timely results.

What are your education credentials? Feel free to add relevant courses and trainings. Click “i” for more information.
Education

List your education, starting with the most recent, and work backwards from there. Include the name of the school, the city where each school you attended is located (secondary and beyond), and the years you completed.

Be sure to list any certificates or diplomas you received, including those for mini-courses like computer or software courses, first aid, or any training that might be useful in the job you are applying for. If a degree is in process, be sure to include it in the CV. If you do not have a college degree, it is important to mention any college level coursework or seminars that might be relevant to the job you are applying for.

Tailor this section based on the specific job description and list your skills and expertise (Optional) . Click “i” for more information.
Skills

This section may be needed as further support to showcase specific skills that would set you apart from other candidates. It is especially useful when the desired position requires experiences from positions throughout one's career. One easy way to determine which areas of expertise to include is to look at several advertisements for positions of interest and note which areas of expertise are listed as desirable.

Group your skills under two or three (no more than five) skill titles such as “community relations”, “customer service”, or “project management”. These can come from paid or unpaid work, or volunteer experience, and even hobbies. If all of your experience is in an unrelated field to the job you’re applying for, focus on the skills you learned that could be applied to the new job you’re applying for.

References

List your references or a note stating that they are available on request.

In case of listing references, list names, addressenes and business affiliations of three persons (not relatives) who are familiar with your work and character. If you are a recent graduate, you can list your teachers. Ask references for permission to use their names. References need to be alerted that they may be getting a phone call from the employer.
